text.p: MSAS Cargo International said its operating profit rose 27 percent in 1996 to 23.7 million pounds, while its turnover rose two percent to 829 million pounds.
The company added in a statement that average air weight per shipment continued to grow and now exceeds 270 kg.

The operating margin rose to 2.9 percent from 2.3 percent and this has now doubled over the last three years. Cash flow again improved despite an increase of more than 20 percent in capital expenditure. Operating profit return on capital employed grew from 34 percent to 39 percent, it added.

The company said the expansion of services covering the full range of supply chain management activities continued and within its overall global margin growth of 12 percent in 1996 airfreight grew by 11 percent, seafreight by 18 percent and logistics services by 46 percent.
It said that new logistics centres were opened in Europe, Asia and America and to meet the needs of its multi-national customers, new subsidiaries were setup in Finland, Korea, and Mexico.
There are plans in 1997 to develop in Brazil, Chile and India in 1997, it added. The Company's growth has been reflected in an increase in its total employees by 400 to 5800.

In the U.S. the weakness in the electronics sector, especially in semi-conductors impacted on sales growth, and export air weight was static. Cost management and margin improvements produced another increase in U.S. operating profit of almost two million pounds, it said.

In South East Asia MSAS improved its overall profitability by 27 percent, led by a seven percent growth in airweight and a 40 percent increase in warehousing and distribution activity. All locations showed profit improverments but the most significant growth was in Singapore. Taiwan, Malaysia and the Philippines.

MSAS said that in contrast inpan and Korea export air weight grew but ground costs also increased due to the establishment of the new Korean company, the restructuring of the Japanese network and the installation of new IT systems.
This resulted in in lower profits in both countries, it added.
Despite difficult economic conditions in much of Europe the major businesses in the UK, Germany and Italy, experienced strong profit growth in all service sectors.

Finland was profitable in its first year of operation and Ireland, Norway and Portugal also showed improved profit performance. MSAS' specialist logistics business in Antwerp more than doubled its operating profit. In other countries the performance was not as good as 1995 but total operating profit in Europe and Africa improved by 28 percent.

MSAS is continuing to invest in information technology. Its global integrated air, sea, road and accounting system went live in four more countries in 1996, and over the next 12 months a further six countries in Europe and Asia will be converted to this system ,it said.
To meet customers' needs for integrated logistics management MSAS are developing systems for purchase order handling, bar code labelling and scanning, it added.

Chief Executive, Doug Ash, said: "1996 was another milestone in our four year plan to achieve a 3 percent operating profit return on sales by 1997. We have more than doubled this key "performance indicator over the last 3 years, during which time our sales have grown by one third and our operating profit has almost tripled." - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
